full_judgment:
5. The learned Advocate-on-record for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the prosecution witnesses made departure from the prosecution case as well as the statement made by the prosecution witnesses earlier and further the High Court Division has not said a single word as how the petitioner is liable for the offence for which he was convicted and thus the present case is virtually a case of no evidence as because not a single prosecution witness has stated anything as to how the petitioner is involved; the High Court Division without at all considering the case of the petitioner that he did not issue any token on that particular time and date, arrived at an erroneous conclusion that the petitioner knowing fully well about the forged bill issued token specially when the prosecution did not take any steps to seize the register and make the same as exhibit and in the absence of strict proof of the fact that the petitioner issued token knowing fully well about the forgery of bills the conviction can not be sustained inasmuch as per Banking Department Manual, token clerk would receive the bills and issue token taking signature of the party but in the present case there is no such evidence to the effect that the petitioner receiving the bill issued token after taking signature of the party and then putting his initial under the same; further it is the case of the prosecution that the petitioner issued token against Advice No. 151 and Index No. 70 whereas it is defence case that the petitioner did not issue the disputed token on that day and on this point "P.W.1 stated that " বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের টোকেন ইস্যুর দায়িত্বে প্রতিদিন কতজন ক্লার্ক নিয়োজিত থাকে বলিতে পারিব না। সত্য নয় যে, এই আসামী ২/৮/৯২ তারিখে কোন টোকেন ইস্যু করেন নাই" and P.W.9 stated that "মাসের প্রথম কয়েকদিন টোকেন ক্লার্কগণ ৩/৪টি কাউন্টারে কাজ করেন। এই মামলার বিতর্কিত চারটি বিল দেখিলে বলিতে পারিব যে, উহার টোকেন ক্লার্ক কে ছিলেন।" and P.W. 23, the then District Anti-Corruption Officer, in his cross-examination stated that:- আসামী এনামুল হক টোকেন ইস্যু করিয়াছেন মর্মে দেখাবার কোন কাগজ জব্দ করা হয় নাই।" but inspite of the above, the petitioner was convicted without fixing his specific liability which has caused a total failure of justice. 

 7. Regarding the question as to whether in the instant case the G.D. Entry, being the first information of a cognizable offence to the police was the FIR, the High Court Division held that there is substance in the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General that Anti Corruption Department took up the matter and they proceeded as per the Anti Corruption Rules and after making preliminary enquiry lodged an F.I.R. and then took up the investigation and that anti corruption cases are treated as special cases and those are governed by the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (Act No. XL of 1958) and also the Anti Corruption Rules which have been framed under section 12 of the Act 1958. 

 9. Regarding the submission that the Agriculture Office and D.A.O. Office committed the forgery, the High Court Division found that since Mirza Saifuddin Hassan, officer of Cash Section of the Bangladesh Bank; in his confessional statement admitted that at the time of payment, Abul Hossain Shah, Deputy Director of the Bangladesh Bank who has also been convicted, came with the party when the token number was called on and he disclosed that the party is his friend and Abul Hossain Shah previously also intimated the Assistant Manager in the box about his payment and he also ordered Mirza Saifuddin Hasan to bring the money and in this way these petitioner and others, in connivance with each other, committed the forgery and withdrew the money for their personal gain and it has also been proved that the petitioner and others prepared forged emboss seal and forged the signatures of the D.A.O and his staff which has been proved by P.W.12 Shamsuddin Firoj, the then D.A.O. Khulna, P.W.14 Md. Din-e-Elahi, Auditor, P.W. 16 Md. Afzal Hossain, Superintendent P.W.20 Auditor Md. Sekandar Ali, P.W.21 Tehura Begum, the hand writing expert, and accordingly the learned Divisional Special Judge, in his judgment, has also discussed the involvement of each of the convicts and the official duties of convicts (1) Md. Badrul Alam (2) Md. Enamul Huq Molla (3) Champak Kumar Biswas (4) Sk. Abul Hossain (5) Mirza Saifuddin Hasan and (6) Shah Abul Hossain who being present ordered for payment claiming the party to be his friend, and so from the evidence it is found that the petitioner and others formed a gang to misappropriate the money from the Government Exchequer of which they are the custodians and the learned Divisional Special Judge, after elaborately discussing the evidence, found the petitioner guilty under section 409/109 and also 417/109 and 472/109 of the Penal Code together with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and from the evidence the charge framed against the petitioner and other under section 409/109, 168/199, 471/109 and 472/109 of the Penal Code together with section 5(2) of the prevention Corruption Act, 1947 having been proved beyond all reasonable doubt and accordingly there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and order of conviction.
